correctness.rationale: The anisotropic norm-one conic has \(q+1\) points. Every nonzero two-sum has one unordered representation because a nondegenerate affine-line section of an anisotropic conic has at most two points, exchanged by subtraction from the sum. The sole multi-pair fiber is zero, producing the exact formula (1) of RESULT.md. The maximization correctly treats the lone unmatched point, yields \(5/3\) for \(q=3\) and \(3-3/(q-1)\) for \(q\ge5\), and equality conditions are all reversible. Orthogonality establishes the normalization. Exact arithmetic checker tests seven field orders including \(9,25\); no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Erasing one point of a norm-one conic is a naturally motivated finite-field Fourier sampling defect. The exact sharp fourth norm, a discontinuous small-field phase transition, and mandatory extinction of the unique surviving antipode for \(q\ge5\) determine genuine sharp loss-of-data geometry absent from field-size-uniform restriction exponents. This sharp complete classification is self-contained and meaningful without a downstream general theorem.
